> [!TRAP] Strict ISO C Note vs Paper Left-to-Right Trace
> Under strict ISO C99/C11 rules, `c = a++ + --b - a++ + b;` invokes **Undefined Behaviour** because variable `a` is modified twice (`a++` and `a++`) between two adjacent sequence points without a defined evaluation order.

- **Conventional Left-to-Right Classroom Paper Trace (`a = 8, b = 4` initially):**
  1. First `a++` yields **`8`** (`a` becomes `9`).
  2. `--b` pre-decrements `b` to `3` and yields **`3`**.
  3. Second `a++` yields **`9`** (`a` becomes `10`).
  4. Final `b` reads current `b` = **`3`**.
  5. Substitute left-to-right: `c = 8 + 3 - 9 + 3 =` **`5`** (with final `a = 10`, `b = 3`, **`c = 5`**; note compilers that delay post-increments until `;` may yield `8 + 3 - 8 + 3 = 6`).

### Part (a) — Storage Classes Used in C

- **Role:** C's four variable storage classes specify **storage location**, **default initial value**, **scope/linkage**, and **lifetime**:

| Storage Class | Storage Location | Initial Value | Scope / Linkage | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auto` | Stack (RAM) | Garbage | Local to block (no linkage) | Until block exits |
| `register` | CPU register (hint) | Garbage | Local to block (`&` illegal) | Until block exits |
| `static` | Data / BSS segment | `0` | Block-local or file-internal | Entire program execution |
| `extern` | Data / BSS segment | `0` | Global across `.c` source files | Entire program execution |

- **Example:** `static int count = 0; count++;` inside a function keeps its incremented value across calls, whereas `auto int count = 0;` resets on every invocation.

### Part (b) — Call by Value vs Call by Address

> [!COMPARE] Call by Value vs Call by Address in C
> | Parameter | Call by Value | Call by Address |
> |---|---|---|
> | **What Is Passed** | Copies of actual argument **values** (`swap(a, b)`). | Memory **addresses** of actual variables (`swap(&a, &b)`). |
> | **Formal Parameters** | Ordinary value variables (`int x, int y`). | Pointer variables (`int *x, int *y`). |
> | **Caller Side Effects** | Changes inside callee **never** alter caller variables. | Dereferencing `*x` directly updates caller variables in place. |
> | **Memory & Return** | Copies full data; returns only one scalar value. | Copies compact addresses; can update multiple caller outputs. |

```c
void byVal(int x)  { x = 50; }       /* caller variable unchanged */
void byAddr(int *p){ *p = 50; }      /* caller variable becomes 50 */
```

### Part (a) — Relation Between Header File and Library File

- **Header File (`.h`):** A human-readable source file included during **preprocessing** (`#include <math.h>`) that supplies **declarations/interfaces**—function prototypes, `#define` macros, and type definitions—so the compiler can type-check calls.
- **Library File (`.a` / `.lib` / `.so` / `.dll`):** A pre-compiled binary archive joined during **linking** (`gcc prog.c -lm`) that contains the actual machine-code **definitions/bodies** of those standard functions (`sqrt()`, `printf()`).

### Part (b) — Operator Precedence and Associativity

- **Operator Precedence:** Determines **which operator binds first** when an unparenthesized expression contains operators from different priority tiers:
  - Example: In `int x = 2 + 3 * 4;`, `*` has higher precedence than `+`, so C evaluates `2 + (3 * 4) = 14` (not `20`).
- **Operator Associativity:** Resolves ties when adjacent operators belong to the **same precedence tier**:
  - **Left-to-Right (`*`, `/`, `%`, `+`, `-`):** `20 / 5 / 2` groups as `(20 / 5) / 2 = 4 / 2 = 2`.
  - **Right-to-Left (`=`, `+=`, unary `!`, `~`, `? :`):** `a = b = 10` groups as `a = (b = 10)`, assigning `10` to `b` and then `10` to `a`.

### Part (c) — Equality (`==`) vs Assignment (`=`) Operator

> [!COMPARE] Equality (`==`) vs Assignment (`=`) in C
> | Parameter | Equality Operator (`==`) | Assignment Operator (`=`) |
> |---|---|---|
> | **Category & Purpose** | Relational operator testing whether two values are equal. | Assignment operator storing RHS value into LHS variable. |
> | **Side Effect** | Does **not** modify either operand (`5 == x` is legal). | Overwrites LHS lvalue (`5 = x` is a compile-time lvalue error). |
> | **Evaluated Result** | Yields integer `1` (true) or `0` (false). | Yields the assigned value stored in LHS (`if (x = 5)` is always true!). |

### Part (a) — Advantages of User-Defined Functions

- **Modularity (Top-Down Decomposition):** Breaks a large, complex program into smaller, single-responsibility sub-modules (`readData()`, `computeTax()`, `printReport()`), keeping `main()` concise.
- **Code Reusability:** Write logic once and invoke it from multiple places without duplicating lines of code.
- **Easier Debugging & Testing:** Bugs are isolated to individual functions whose inputs and outputs can be tested independently.
- **Team Collaboration & Maintainability:** Different programmers can implement separate functions simultaneously as long as prototypes are agreed upon.

### Part (b) — Function Declaration vs Function Definition

> [!COMPARE] Function Declaration (Prototype) vs Function Definition in C
> | Parameter | Function Declaration (Prototype) | Function Definition |
> |---|---|---|
> | **Purpose** | Tells the compiler the function's name, return type, and parameter types. | Supplies the actual executable statements (body) of the function. |
> | **Syntax & Semicolon** | Ends with a semicolon `;` and has no `{}` body: `int add(int, int);` | Followed by a compound `{ ... }` block with no header semicolon. |
> | **Memory Allocation** | Allocates **zero** machine-code storage; may appear multiple times. | Generates compiled code; must appear **exactly once** (One Definition Rule). |

### Part (c) — Actual Parameters and Formal Parameters with Example

- **Actual Parameters (Arguments):** Values, variables, or expressions passed inside parentheses at the **function call site** (`sum = add(num, 10);`).
- **Formal Parameters:** Local typed variables listed in the **function definition header** (`int add(int a, int b)`) that receive copies of the actual arguments upon invocation.

```c
#include <stdio.h>
int add(int a, int b) {         /* a, b = formal parameters */
    return a + b;
}
int main(void) {
    int x = 7;
    printf("%d\n", add(x, 5));  /* x, 5 = actual parameters -> prints 12 */
    return 0;
}
```

> [!MARKS] 4 + 4 = 8 Marks (`a`: Four C storage classes with example — 4m · `b`: Call by Value vs Call by Reference — 4m)

### Part (a) — Storage Classes in C

- **Role:** A storage class determines a variable's **storage location**, **default initial value**, **visibility (scope)**, and **lifetime**:

| Storage Class | Storage Location | Default Initial Value | Scope | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auto` | Stack (RAM) | Garbage (indeterminate) | Local to block | Until enclosing block exits |
| `register` | CPU register (or stack) | Garbage (indeterminate) | Local to block | Until enclosing block exits (`&` address-of illegal) |
| `static` | Data/BSS segment | `0` | Block (local) or file (internal linkage) | Entire program execution |
| `extern` | Data/BSS segment | `0` | Global across translation units | Entire program execution |

```c
#include <stdio.h>
extern int shared_cfg;          /* declared here; defined in another file */
void counter(void) {
    auto int local = 1;         /* recreated every call */
    static int calls = 0;       /* persists across calls */
    printf("local=%d, calls=%d\n", local, ++calls);
}
```

### Part (b) — Call by Value vs Call by Reference

> [!COMPARE] Call by Value vs Call by Reference in C
> | Parameter | Call by Value | Call by Reference (Address Passing) |
> |---|---|---|
> | **What Is Passed** | Copies of actual argument **values** (`swap(x, y)`). | Memory **addresses** (pointers) of actual variables (`swap(&x, &y)`). |
> | **Caller Modification** | Changes to formal parameters **do not** affect caller variables. | Dereferencing (`*p`) modifies the caller's original variables directly. |
> | **Memory Overhead** | Separate local copy created for each argument. | Copies only fixed-size pointer addresses (`4` or `8` bytes). |
> | **Multiple Outputs** | Can return at most one scalar value via `return`. | Can update multiple caller variables simultaneously. |

```c
void by_val(int x)  { x = 99; }       /* caller variable unchanged */
void by_ref(int *p) { *p = 99; }      /* caller variable becomes 99 */
```
